drawings.description: sous les mots encerclés « Topos non cohérent », un croquis : deux ovales « $Z'$ » et « $Z''$ » qui se recouvrent, la région commune marquée « $I$ » ; au-dessus, entre les deux, « $W$ » ; au-dessous, un trait terminé par une pointe vers le bas.
drawings.kind: two overlapping ovals with a marked intersection, two braces labelled w and v
drawings.notes: Two ovals overlapping: Z' on the left, Z'' on the right (tilted, rising to the right), I in the common region; above them, between the two, W, with a stroke running from it down into the common region. Redrawn 2026-11-13 after the editor's answer (#148: « c'est bien mais les traits à côté de w et v (minuscules) sont des accolades »): the small letter above W at the left is a lowercase w, and the wavy stroke beside it is a brace; the mark under the ovals is a lowercase v (not an arrow head), and the short curved stroke above it, leaving the common region, is a brace. Both braces are drawn as plain brace curves, their tips towards the letters' side as far as the page shows; their exact extent is a reading. Partial: the wavy scribbles inside Z' (left of I) and inside Z'' (right of I) are still not drawn (they may be further braces or small illegible labels); the stroke from W is drawn as one curve where the page has two passes. The ringed words above (Topos non cohérent) are not drawn. Overlaid on the 400 dpi colour crop. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): not compiled (no TeX in the session); the TikZ rasterised and laid over the 350 dpi colour render of the scan, with ink/pencil separations of the crop. The two ovals, I and the brace by v lie on the ink to within about 1 unit and were kept. Changed: the brace by w starts at the top of the right arm of W (it was drawn from the w itself) and runs as a wave to its downturned end; w, W and the end of the stroke from W placed on their ink. The wavy scribbles left out before are now drawn as the strokes they are, without reading them: inside Z', left of I, a wavy stroke with four short downstrokes; inside Z'', right of I, a wavy stroke with three; under them, a long wavy stroke from the right of Z'' down to a dip at about (54, 45) and on to the crossing under I. Each may be a brace or a small word; the page does not settle it. Every element lies on the ink to within about 1 unit; the stroke from W, gone over twice in its middle, is drawn once. The ringed words above (Topos non cohérent) are text.
drawings.disagreement: The transcription reads « au-dessous, un trait terminé par une pointe vers le bas »: by the editor (#148) the stroke is a brace and the mark under it the letter v; the lowercase w above W and its brace are not in the transcription.
